ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, Table 2 is a table of “region—harvest start time,” listing Shandong as May 26, Hubei as May 18, Beijing as June 12, and Jilin as July 13. In the table, Hubei's harvest start time is in mid-May, while Beijing and Jilin, which have higher latitudes and relatively poorer heat conditions, have harvest times delayed in sequence to June and July. Then reason: Tibet belongs to a high-altitude region, with insufficient heat conditions, so wheat maturity usually will be delayed. Compared with Hubei, which is low-altitude, has relatively sufficient heat, and starts harvesting on May 18 in the table, Tibet's wheat harvest time should be after Hubei. Therefore, the harvesting time of wheat in Tibet is later than in Hubei.
